components.note: 耂 (old) — the earliest sense of 考 was an elderly, deceased father, which is why this part is 'old'
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.english: I have a math exam tomorrow.
example.fact: 考 is used both for taking and giving tests: 考试 (exam), 考虑 (to consider), 考古 (archaeology), 高考 (the national college entrance exam, a huge event in China), 考研 (to sit the graduate entrance exam).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — acting with the hands
争 (zhēng) — 'to strive', and it gives the sound

example.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè zhèng yí wàn kuài.
example.english: He earns ten thousand yuan a month.
example.fact: 挣钱 means to earn money, and 赚钱 means the same; 挣 is more colloquial. Read zhēng, 挣 means to struggle free, as in 挣扎 (to struggle) and 挣脱 (to break loose).

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the sun sinking into the grass
日 (sun) — the sun in the middle of the lower part, marking dusk

example.english: Could it be that he is ill?
example.fact: 莫 was originally 'dusk' (the sun setting in the grass), and the later character 暮 took over that meaning. As a word it is a classical 'not/no one' that survives in 莫非 (could it be), 莫名其妙 (baffling) and 莫斯科 (Moscow).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — plants covering something
冡 gives the sound méng and has the idea of covering

example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu méngzhù le yǎnjing.
example.english: She covered her eyes with her hands.
example.fact: 蒙 is méng for 'cover' (蒙面, 启蒙 'enlightenment', 蒙受 'to suffer, receive'). Read mēng it means to trick or guess, as in 蒙人 and 蒙对了. Read Měng, it is the Mongols: 蒙古 (Mongolia).

components.note: 欠 (open mouth) — a breath and mouth radical with no link to the meaning here
区 (qū) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā míngnián xiǎng qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: He wants to travel to Europe next year.
example.fact: 欧 is a shortened form of 欧洲 (Europe), which came from the sound of 'Europa' (欧罗巴). It builds 欧元 (euro) and 欧美 (Europe and America). Gamers also use 欧 as slang for lucky streaks.

excludeSuggestion: Used almost only as an abbreviation or in transliterated names (Europe) or as a surname.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's limbs
申 (shēn) gives the sound — identical in pinyin, and it also meant 'to extend'

example.english: Please stretch out your hand.
example.fact: 伸 means to stretch or extend: 伸手 (reach out a hand), 伸懒腰 (to stretch lazily). The idiom 能屈能伸 means being able to bend and to stretch, that is, flexible and resilient in good and bad times.

components.note: 立 — the top part, a distorted echo of the strokes of 言 (speech)
日 — here a squashed 口 (mouth), not the sun

example.english: I like listening to music.
example.fact: 音 means sound, especially pitch and pronunciation: 音乐 (music), 发音 (pronunciation), 口音 (accent), 拼音 (pinyin, 'spell-sound'). 声音 is the everyday word for sound or voice.

components.note: 力 (strength) — physical force
又 replaced 巠 of the traditional 勁 in simplification — a stand-in with no real sound link

example.english: He works with a lot of energy.
example.fact: 劲 is the colloquial word for strength and vigor: 有劲 (energetic, or fun), 没劲 (boring, or without energy), 使劲 (to exert effort). Read jìng, it is an adjective meaning 'strong', as in 强劲 (powerful).

components.note: 心 (heart) — wickedness of the heart
亚 (yà) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: The weather today is terrible.
example.fact: 恶 is read è in 恶劣 (awful), 恶意 (malice), 罪恶 (crime), 恶作剧 (a prank). Read ě in 恶心 (nauseating, to feel sick) and wù, it means to hate: 厌恶.

components.note: 立 (stand) — standing at the side
方 (fāng) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ang ending

example.english: He is sitting next to me.
example.fact: 旁 builds 旁边 (beside), 路旁 (roadside) and 旁人 (bystander). In studying characters, 偏旁 is the word for a radical or component, using 旁 for 'side'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling by hand
犮 (bá) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ cǎo bá diào le.
example.english: He pulled up the weeds.
example.fact: 拔 is to yank something out: 拔草 (weed), 拔牙 (extract a tooth), 拔河 (tug of war, literally 'pull river'). 挺拔 describes something tall and straight.

components.note: 冎 (bone) — the jointed bone shape
⺼ (flesh) — flesh surrounding the bone

example.english: His leg is broken.
example.fact: 骨 is bone: 骨头 (bone), 骨折 (fracture), 排骨 (ribs, a popular dish). It also gives the idea of backbone: 骨气 is moral courage, and 骨肉 means one's flesh and blood.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house
玉 (jade) — a treasure kept in the house

example.hanzi: 这个孩子是全家的宝贝。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi shì quán jiā de bǎobèi.
example.english: This child is the whole family's treasure.
example.fact: 宝 is a treasure: 宝石 (gem), 国宝 (national treasure, such as the giant panda). 宝贝 and 宝宝 are affectionate words for children and for a lover. The e-commerce site Taobao (淘宝) is 'hunt for treasure'.

components.note: 走 (walk) — the old sense is hurrying toward something
取 (qǔ) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: This book is very interesting.
example.fact: 趣 mainly appears in 有趣 (interesting), 兴趣 (interest), 乐趣 (pleasure) and 趣事 (an amusing anecdote). The sentence 对…感兴趣 means to be interested in something.

components.note: 女 (woman) — mother's milk
乃 (nǎi) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.hanzi: 我每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang hē yì bēi niúnǎi.
example.english: I drink a glass of milk every morning.
example.fact: 奶 means milk: 牛奶 (cow's milk), 奶茶 (milk tea), 奶酪 (cheese). Doubled, 奶奶 is the term for a father's mother, whereas 外婆 is a mother's mother.

components.note: 目 (eye) — opening the eyes
争 (zhēng) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.english: He slowly opened his eyes.
example.fact: 睁 is used only for opening the eyes, the opposite of 闭 (bì). The idiom 睁一只眼闭一只眼 means 'open one eye, close the other', that is, to look the other way and let something pass.

components.note: A mound of earth rising from the ground line, or a lump of clay.

example.pinyin: Huā xūyào zhòng zài tǔ lǐ.
example.english: Flowers need to be planted in soil.
example.fact: 土 is earth: 泥土 (soil), 土地 (land), 土豆 (potato, literally 'earth bean'). It is also one of the Five Elements. As an adjective, 土 means unfashionable or countrified: 很土 is 'so uncool'.

components.note: Often explained as a hand holding an axe or tool, the symbol of the head of a household.

example.pinyin: Tā hé fùqīn yìqǐ qù diàoyú.
example.english: He went fishing with his father.
example.fact: 父 is a formal and written 'father': 父亲 is the formal term and 爸爸 the everyday one. It builds 父母 (parents) and 祖父 (paternal grandfather). 父 can also be read fǔ in a few old terms of respect for men.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the meaning part; its link to 'post' is historical
只 (zhī) gives a loose sound hint — shared vowel, different tone

example.english: His profession is a doctor.
example.fact: 职 appears in job words: 职业 (profession), 职位 (position), 职员 (staff), 辞职 (to resign), 升职 (to be promoted), 职责 (duty). It does not usually stand alone.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — spoken words
荒 (huāng) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ shuō huǎng le.
example.english: He lied to me.
example.fact: 谎 is a lie: 说谎 (tell a lie), 撒谎 (tell lies), 谎话 (lie), 谎言 (falsehood). 善意的谎言 is a white lie.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden pole
干 (gān) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Qígān shàng guà zhe yí miàn hóngqí.
example.english: A red flag is hanging on the flagpole.
example.fact: 杆 is a long pole: 旗杆 (flagpole), 电线杆 (utility pole), 钓鱼杆 (fishing rod). Read gǎn, it is a barrel or stalk, as in 笔杆 (pen barrel) and a measure word for rifles (一杆枪).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — bitter herbs
古 (gǔ) gives a loose sound hint — shared vowel, different tone

example.english: This medicine is very bitter.
example.fact: 苦 is bitter, but also hardship: 吃苦 ('eat bitterness') means to endure hardship. 辛苦 is 'hard work', and 辛苦了 is how you thank someone for their effort. 苦瓜 is bitter melon.

components.note: 米 (rice) — grain
斗 (dipper) — a measure, originally used to measure grain

example.english: Please get the materials ready.
example.fact: 料 means raw material and stuff: 材料 (material), 饮料 (drink), 资料 (data), 调料 (seasoning), 料理 (cuisine, as in 日本料理). It can also mean 'to expect': 出乎意料 is 'beyond expectation'.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old sense is a small stalk or stick
攵 (tap) — holding a stick, to count off one by one

example.pinyin: Tā dédào le yì méi jīnpái.
example.english: He won a gold medal.
example.fact: 枚 is a formal measure word for small, flat or compact items: 一枚硬币 (a coin), 一枚戒指 (a ring), 一枚奖牌 (a medal), 一枚导弹 (a missile). The idiom 不胜枚举 means 'too many to list one by one'.

meanings: sentence-final particle for a cheerful announcement

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken particle
娄 (lóu) gives the sound — close, differing only in tone

example.english: Dinner's ready!
example.fact: 喽 is a lively sentence-final particle, roughly a blend of 了 and 哦, used to announce something: 走喽 (off we go). It is also read lóu in 喽啰 (minions, henchmen in a bandit gang), where 喽 has its own history.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — a cliff face
口 — a rock at the foot of the cliff

example.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu hěn duō dà shítou.
example.english: There are lots of big rocks by the river.
example.fact: 石 is stone: 石头 (stone), 石油 (petroleum, 'rock oil'), 钻石 (diamond), 化石 (fossil). Read dàn, 石 was an old unit of grain, about 100 liters; 石 is also a surname.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a wet substance being spread
余 (yú) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā zài qiáng shàng tú le yì céng qī.
example.english: He applied a coat of paint to the wall.
example.fact: 涂 is to spread something on a surface: 涂药 (apply ointment), 涂改 (to alter by erasing), 涂鸦 (graffiti, 'smeared crows'). 糊涂 means confused or muddled.

components.note: 走 (walk) — chasing, hurrying along
㐱 (zhěn) gives a loose sound hint

example.english: Eat it while it's hot.
example.fact: 趁 means to take advantage of a moment: 趁热 (while hot), 趁早 (as early as possible), 趁机 (seize the opportunity), 趁年轻 (while young). 趁火打劫 is 'to rob a house on fire', that is, to profit from someone's trouble.

components.note: 夫 — here read as a hand shape, letting something slip
丿 (slash) — something slipping away

example.english: He lost his job.
example.fact: 失 is a more formal and abstract 'lose': 失去 (to lose), 失败 (to fail), 失望 (disappointed), 失业 (unemployed), 失眠 (insomnia). For misplacing objects, speakers say 丢 (diū).

components.note: 刂 (knife) — scraping with a blade
舌 (shé) gives a loose sound hint

example.english: It's very windy outside.
example.fact: 刮 is to scrape, shave, or blow: 刮风 (the wind blows), 刮胡子 (shave), 刮痧 (gua sha, a scraping therapy). The idiom 刮目相看 means to look at someone with new eyes.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — colors of dyed silk
录 (lù) gives the sound — close, differing in vowel

example.hanzi: 春天来了,树叶都变绿了。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, shùyè dōu biàn lǜ le.
example.english: Spring has come and the leaves have turned green.
example.fact: 绿 is green: 绿色, 绿灯 (green light), 绿茶 (green tea). It carries a famous cultural twist: 戴绿帽子 ('wear a green hat') means to have an unfaithful partner, so avoid giving green hats. It is read lù in 绿林 and 鸭绿江 (the Yalu River).

components.note: 灬 (fire) — cooking over heat
者 (zhě) gives a loose sound hint — close, differing in the vowel and tone

example.english: I'm cooking noodles.
example.fact: 煮 is cooking in water: 煮饭, 煮面, 煮鸡蛋. Cooking methods are distinct in Chinese: 煮 boil, 炒 stir-fry, 蒸 steam. 煮豆燃萁, 'burning bean stalks to cook beans', is an idiom for family members harming one another.

components.note: 凵 (pit) — a trap or container
乂 (cross mark) — a mark of danger inside the pit

example.english: That dog is fierce.
example.fact: 凶 means fierce, or unlucky: 凶手 (murderer), 吉凶 (good or bad fortune), 他很凶 (he is harsh). Beware the homophones 兄 (older brother) and 胸 (chest).

components.note: 缶 (earthenware jar) — the old sense is a chipped or broken pot
夬 (guài) gives a loose sound hint

example.english: There is a shortage of water here.
example.fact: 缺 is to lack: 缺少 (be short of), 缺点 (shortcoming, the opposite of 优点), 缺席 (to be absent), 缺钱 (short of money). 缺德 literally 'lack virtue' means mean or immoral.

components.note: 水 (water, shown as 氺) — smooth flow
大 — the large shape above, completing the old image of safe passage

example.english: I went to Thailand last year.
example.fact: 泰 means peaceful: 泰然 (calm), 国泰民安 ('the country is at peace, the people safe'). It shortens 泰国 (Thailand), and 泰山 is the sacred Mount Tai, which is also a polite term for one's father-in-law.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling apart by hand
斥 (chì) gives a loose sound hint — shared -i ending

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiù fángzi chāi le.
example.english: He tore down the old house.
example.fact: 拆 is to take apart or demolish: 拆开 (unwrap, open up), 拆除 (remove), 拆迁 (demolish and relocate, common in urban development), 拆礼物 (unwrap gifts). 拆台 means to sabotage someone's efforts.

components.note: The simplified form uses the central part 朮 of the traditional 術, so the tree-like shape here is a stand-in, not a meaning about trees.

example.pinyin: Tā zuò le yí gè shǒushù.
example.english: He had an operation.
example.fact: 术 means skill or technique: 技术 (technology), 艺术 (art), 手术 (surgery), 魔术 (magic), 学术 (academic), 武术 (martial arts). It almost never stands alone.

components.note: Often explained as three 十 (tens) joined together, a 30-year generation.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì shìjiè shàng zuì gāo de shān.
example.english: This is the highest mountain in the world.
example.fact: 世 means a generation or lifetime: 世界 (world), 世纪 (century), 世代 (generations), 去世 (to pass away) and 一世 (a whole lifetime). The idea of 'three tens' in its shape is a commonly told explanation.

components.note: 阝 (city) — a place or town
君 (jūn) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.english: The Han dynasty set up many commanderies.
example.fact: 郡 was an administrative unit under the Qin and Han dynasties, above the 县 (county), forming the 郡县制 system. In Japan and Korea it survives as 'county' (gun).

excludeSuggestion: Historical administrative term; rare as a modern standalone word.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — a plant
早 (zǎo) gives the sound — close, differing in the initial

example.pinyin: Cǎodì shàng yǒu hěn duō huā.
example.english: There are many flowers on the lawn.
example.fact: 草 builds 草地 (lawn), 草原 (grassland), 草莓 (strawberry) and 草稿 (rough draft). It can also mean careless: 草率 (hasty, sloppy).

components.note: 辶 (walk) — encountering something on the way
曹 (cáo) gives the sound — close, differing in initial and tone

example.english: He was turned down.
example.fact: 遭 is for encountering something bad: 遭到 (to be subjected to), 遭遇 (to encounter), 遭殃 (to suffer disaster). It also counts trips: 走一遭 means to make a round trip.

components.note: 缶 (earthenware jar) — a container
雚 (guàn) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yí guàn kělè.
example.english: There is a can of cola on the table.
example.fact: 罐 is both a container and a measure word: 罐头 (canned food), 易拉罐 (pull-tab can), 茶叶罐 (tea caddy). 拔罐 is cupping, a traditional therapy using heated glass cups.

components.note: 米 (rice) — sticky rice was used as glue
占 (zhān) gives the sound — identical in pinyin

example.pinyin: Qǐng yòng jiāoshuǐ bǎ zhǐ zhān shàng.
example.english: Please stick the paper on with glue.
example.fact: 粘 is the verb 'to stick': 粘贴 (paste, as in 复制粘贴 copy and paste), 粘住 (to stick to). Read nián, it is a variant of 黏 for 'sticky'. It is also a surname, Niàn.

components.note: 女 (woman) — originally linked to 'delicate, fine'
少 (shǎo) gives a loose sound hint — shared -ao ending

example.english: What a brilliant idea!
example.fact: 妙 means wonderful or ingenious: 奇妙 (marvelous), 美妙 (beautiful), 巧妙 (clever), 妙招 (a clever trick). 不妙 means 'not good' and 莫名其妙 means baffling.

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand beside water
少 (shǎo) — 'few, small' for the small grains, and a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上玩沙子。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng wán shāzi.
example.english: The children are playing in the sand on the beach.
example.fact: 沙 builds 沙子 (sand), 沙滩 (beach) and 沙漠 (desert). It also stands in for sounds: 沙发 (sofa) and 沙拉 (salad). Describing a voice as 沙哑 means hoarse.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo was a writing material; the link to 'answer' is historical
合 (hé) — 'to match, fit', as an answer fits a question

example.english: Please answer this question.
example.fact: 答 is read dá for answering: 回答 (answer), 答案 (answer key), 答题 (to answer questions). In 答应, 'to agree, promise', it is read dā, a classic reading pitfall.

components.note: The upper strokes sit over 冏; the old origin is unclear, so it is best learned as a unit.

example.hanzi: 他在北京开了一家商店。
example.pinyin: Tā zài Běijīng kāi le yì jiā shāngdiàn.
example.english: He opened a shop in Beijing.
example.fact: 商 builds 商店 (shop), 商人 (merchant), 商业 (commerce), 商量 (to discuss). It also means 'quotient' in math. The Shang dynasty has the same character, and tradition says its people, after the fall, became traders.

components.note: 尚 (shàng) gives a loose sound hint
云 stands in for 旨 (tasty) from the traditional 嘗, so the taste idea is no longer visible

example.english: Have a taste of this dish.
example.fact: 尝 is to taste: 尝尝 (try a bit), 品尝 (to savor), 尝试 (to try out). In literary speech 何尝 and 未尝 are rhetorical, as in 我何尝不想? ('how could I not want to?').

components.note: 口 (two mouths) — loud shouting
马 (mǎ) gives the sound — close, differing in tone

example.pinyin: Māma mà le wǒ yí dùn.
example.english: Mom scolded me.
example.fact: 骂 is to scold or swear: 骂人 (to swear at someone), 责骂 (to reproach), 挨骂 or 被骂 (to be scolded). 顿 is the measure word for a scolding, a meal, or a beating.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — shielding with the hands
户 (hù) gives the sound — identical in pinyin, and it means 'door, household'

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎohù hǎo nǐ de yǎnjing.
example.english: Please protect your eyes.
example.fact: 护 appears in 保护 (to protect), 爱护 (to cherish), 护士 (nurse, 'protecting person') and 护照 (passport, 'protecting document'). 护肤 means skincare.
